verdict.tagline: Endless procedural dread with tightly tuned room-by-room combat.
for_you_if: you enjoy deep item synergy and high replay value
you want a crawler that runs smoothly on modest hardware
not_for_you_if: you expect an in-game tutorial to explain mechanics
you rely on stable and bug-free online multiplayer
you dislike a slow start before the game opens up

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks an in-game tutorial or guide for explaining mechanics.

citations.review_text: Very addictive but has basically no tutorial. besides not being beginner friendly its a peak game

Very fun roguelite! The game's utter objection to explaining mechanics can be frustrating for new players, but it's personally endearing. It reminds me of playing Minecraft back in 2012 and having no idea what the hell I'm doing due to the lack of an in-game guide.

citations.review_text: One of the greatest games ever made. It runs on just about anything.

This game is really good basically no limit to replay value. Super hard and in depth im pretty sure this will last you a life time well worth the price. Plays well with low tier hardware too which is always a plus. Basically if youve got any half modern igpu this game is stable. One of the best buys on steam and also like i said basically infinite replay value.

It's a great game but it didn't click for me for the first 10 or so hours. It's difficult to get into and there's not really a tutorial, you just have to put your head down and figure it out. The DLC is very worthwhile and really makes this game something you can put the hours into, and polishes everything well. Could be played on your mom's laptop from 2009.
I am completly hooked on isaac and it is AMAZING i love it so much! And it is easy to run ive been playing on a labtop.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe online multiplayer as laggy and buggy.

citations.review_text: This game is very good for the price when it goes on sale. Although, after a while this game is a snooze fest and gets boring. Not to mention how edgy it is like all the poop just ends up being corny. People say this game is insane for the amount of content and replayability, but having tons of items doesn't mean much when the actual gameplay loop is super boring and stale. The problem I think is the rooms get really repetitive and dying over and over is so miserable because of the amount of shit rng there is. I think overall I understand why other people like it but its just not for me. Playing a lot of the multiplayer made the game way worse too, it is horrible and buggy. ITS OVERATED!
Fairly addictive game. Great fun to play with friends, or alone. (Make sure you have a strong wifi connection if playing online with others, a bit of lag will make your game much harder)

single_points.text: One reviewer says that some characters don't really explain how to unlock them in-game and won't appear on the character selection screen until unlocked.

citation.review_text:
The Binding of Isaac is a game I genuinely enjoy and one of the few games I've been playing for years. No matter how long I take a break, I always find myself coming back to it.

I think it's an excellent roguelike, with a great balance between gameplay and progression. The game gradually becomes more challenging as you progress, without making the early runs feel overwhelmingly difficult.

One of its strongest aspects is the meta-progression. It is very well distributed, gradually introducing more options and mechanics the further you get into the game. This makes it accessible for new players without overwhelming them with too many choices right from the start.

I personally enjoy going through all three stages of progression: early game, mid game and late game. Each has its own appeal and gives you something to work towards.

On top of that, the game has a surprisingly deep lore for those who enjoy exploring it. However, understanding the lore isn't necessary to enjoy the gameplay itself.

The only downside I can think of is that some characters don't really explain how to unlock them in-game. You also won't see them in the character selection screen when starting a run until you've unlocked them. There are only three characters this really applies to: The Lost, The Forgotten and The Keeper.

The Keeper is something you'll eventually unlock through normal progression, particularly by playing Ultra Greed mode, so he's not much of an issue.

The Lost and The Forgotten, however, are much more hidden. You probably won't unlock them naturally unless you already know what you're looking for.

To unlock The Lost, you need to die in a Sacrifice Room while holding the Missing Poster trinket. The Forgotten is considerably more complicated, and explaining the entire process here would take too long. I'd recommend checking The Binding of Isaac Wiki if you want to know how to unlock him. It's not necessarily difficult, but it is quite tedious.
